orgDesign.companyProfile: Amsterdam-based one-click photo book company modeled on PastBook, founded in 2012 in the Rockstart Accelerator by Stefano Cutello (former eBay tech lead) and backed by Vortex Capital Partners since the EUR 350k seed round of December 2015 and the USD 2M convertible note of September 2017. Wouter Staatsen has been CEO since 23 April 2020 (former CEO of Albelli, VP at Cimpress, board advisor since 2018); founder Stefano Cutello is Chief Product & Innovation Officer and owns the patent-pending curation technology that lays out a book in under 60 seconds; Daniel Scheijen (former Albelli country manager) is CMO. Consumers pay per printed product - Small Hardcover from USD 19.99, Large Hardcover from USD 34.99, calendars and posters - in seven currencies and ten site languages; about 80 percent of customers are in the United States, then Australia, Europe and the UK; 10M+ books have been created since 2012 and the app has 1M+ downloads with a Trustpilot TrustScore of 4.5 from 35,837 reviews. The careers page names about 16 core people and LinkedIn places colleagues in Amsterdam, Milan, Vilnius, New York, Colombo (a tech team with Gapstars since October 2025) and New Delhi; 24/7 support runs from the Netherlands, the United States, Sri Lanka and India. Printing is done by partner facilities on four continents, most orders in the country of the customer, shipping to 150+ countries - so the company owns software, curation, marketing and care, not presses. The organisation is modeled at about 75 people including outsourced support agents and engineering pods; no headcount figure here is an official PastBook number.
orgDesign.operatingModel: With about 75 people the company is a consumer software business wrapped around a print-partner network, not a printer with an app: three groups and ten teams. Product and Engineering, led by the CPIO with a lead architect, is six small teams of four to seven people spread over Amsterdam, Vilnius, Milan and the Colombo pod with Gapstars: stream-aligned teams own the mobile app, the web creator with its Facebook and cloud-drive imports and the editor, and the commerce funnel from catalog to order; a complicated-subsystem team owns the curation engine - quality scoring, duplicate removal, moment grouping, best-photo selection and automatic layout - which is the differentiator against on-device memories features and competitor AI studios; and two platform teams provide print-ready rendering, preflight, routing, partner integration and shipping on one side and identity, media storage, privacy and deletion, analytics and the integration gateway to Meta, Dropbox, Google Drive, payment providers, carriers and app stores on the other. Operations and Customer Care is the largest group by headcount: a lean production-operations team of partner managers and quality analysts that runs the facilities on four continents as a utility with routing rules, SLAs and holiday-peak capacity, and a 24/7 support team of agents in the Netherlands, New York, Colombo and New Delhi on WhatsApp, e-mail and chat who resolve order changes, tracking questions, reprints and refunds and answer every negative Trustpilot review within 48 hours. Growth and Brand, under the CMO, owns performance marketing, App Store optimisation, CRM and the Year in Review campaign that drives the Q4 peak, plus an enabling brand, content and localisation team that keeps ten languages, seven currencies, reviews and the sustainability story coherent. Because support agents, marketers and the production manager are themselves customers of the platform (csup, gmkt, opsm), a routing failure at a partner, a blurry page that the curation engine let through or a promo code that does not apply reaches the owning product team the same day. Dependencies run consumer to provider only: product teams consume curation, commerce and platform services; operations and growth consume the bricks the product teams own; every team is owner of the data assets its bricks create so that personal photos, consent records and print files stay traceable and are deleted when the customer asks.

Led from Amsterdam with engineers in Vilnius, Milan and the Colombo pod with Gapstars; its job is to make the one-click promise true for more sources and more products while keeping personal photos safe.
